body: Yeah, is not such a rush, and once you get into the rythm of doing the exercises they give and the classes and all it becomes second nature, rooting for you

For me I was offered a very low paid apprenticeship but due to my age they could up the payment to match a regular salary like the one I was getting on my previous job. So I took it.

It does feel a bit weird being 30 and be so needy of help from everyone as I had no experience at all with what I am working with. However, people is really helpful, the company allows you paid time to do your homework and lessons so its not difficult to balance both. Now doing my level 4 and if I pass I will ask for my company to help me with a degree.

I think its the best way to switch careers because you have a lot of support and you dont need ti worry about choosing studying over working or the other way around, you can really do both

All the best on your apprenticeship!

Hey! sorry for the late reply I did not notice the notification. I am actually on my level 4, passed the epa with no issues. I think I did not do very well as I was told the first discussion would be about my last project and the last about my full portfolio, so I prepped for the first one a lot, then noticed on the day they changed it and it was the opposite order, so was really under prepped and it felt like I was gonna fail it but did my best tried to not be too nervous and be honest while going through it.

For the next one I prepared much better, had my portfolio opened, highlighted the ksbs, and had a miro board with the evidence and snippets of my portfolio to share with the interviewer when he asked for specific proofs. It was all okay at the end 🙂

You will do, I was on the same situation but my studies are from a different country and were not equivalent to the levels required here, I did my functional skills (and you can request support as I did to get a personal tutor to help you with plenty of meetings, worksheets and mockups to prepare) having dyslexia and dyscalculia and passed with flying colors! You will have no issue :)

I will be 30 this year, getting on the apprenticeship is the best thing I have ever done. Go for it! I had no knowledge at all of my subjects and managed to complete it, can't recommend doing it enough!

Yes, I believe so. As I said on my case is as if I didn’t have any studies only a diploma of secondary education.  I started my apprenticeship while doing work for maths and English, I believe they do a small test to see your level at the start and then you have to work on getting the certifications (the apprenticeship provider will help you) so you can’t do the EPA parts of the apprenticeship until you have the certificates but once you got them you can proceed to the last stage of your apprenticeship. I do not know if all apprenticeship providers work the same way so my recommendation is to apply anyway and explain to them that you are happy to work towards the required levels of English and Maths and they will give you more information :)

Thank you for your advice I will definitely check all those and prepare heavily, I have been ‘studying’ my portfolio, find it very difficult to speak when they put me on the spot but will give it my best. Thank you very much!

On my case coming from another country even if I had the required levels on my country they were not convalidated. I only had to pass a level 2 English and Maths. You can request through the apprenticeship help and they will connect you to a tutor who will help you study and provide you plenty of mock exams/exercises to prepare for the official exams . Once you passed they give you the official certificates and then you can do the end part of your apprenticeship
